page: Microsoft Azure E20ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 20 dedicated vCPUs derived from 10 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 160.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio.

This virtual machine runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and includes 1181 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It is also Premium Storage capable, allowing for high-performance external disk attachments. The inclusion of local NVMe storage provides high-speed scratch space, though users must manage data persistence tradeoffs inherent to ephemeral local disks.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2153.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.28 GB/sec. Image and text processing benchmarks also rank in the strong tier. Multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics generally align with average mid-tier performance, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 14717.0 and a large-block memory read bandwidth of 150.84 GB/sec. Notably, the hardware achieves top-tier performance in small-model LLM text generation, reaching 393.88 tokens per second for a 135M parameter model.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and built-in NVMe storage, the E20ds_v6 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads without requiring a transition to more expensive, specialized hardware classes. It is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and software compilation tasks.
